title: Monthly resource and job movement differ by work-limiting status
source_unit: identified 2025 SIPP person, adjacent reference-month pair, conditioned on work-limiting status at month t
variance_method: Fay BRR, 240 replicate weights, perturbation factor 0.5

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month t resource band to month t+1 job-count change; work-limiting status = yes

denominator.unit: valid adjacent person-month pairs with positive person weight and a documented work-limiting condition

below_1x_job_count_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.206 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 0.665–1.472

1_to_2x_job_count_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.138 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 0.695–1.236

2_to_4x_job_count_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.144 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 0.912–1.478

4x_or_more_job_count_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.161 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 1.129–1.761

observations.method: Same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag using monthly THINCPOV and RMNUMJOBS, conditioned on EDISABL=yes; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Census Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals quantify design-based sampling uncertainty for the selected person-month pair universe; the comparison does not identify health onset, accommodation, employer choice, hours, pay, or causality.
observations.subgroup: Persons reporting a work-limiting condition in the first month
observations.counterinterpretation: The pattern may reflect selection, job access, household resources, reporting, or changes outside the observed job count.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month t resource band to month t+1 job-count change; work-limiting status = no

denominator.unit: valid adjacent person-month pairs with positive person weight and no reported work-limiting condition

below_1x_job_count_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.206 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 2.843–3.652

1_to_2x_job_count_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.132 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 1.651–2.169

2_to_4x_job_count_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.075 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 1.577–1.871

4x_or_more_job_count_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.057 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 1.524–1.746

observations.method: Same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag using monthly THINCPOV and RMNUMJOBS, conditioned on EDISABL=no; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Census Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: The work-limiting and non-limiting groups may differ in age, occupation, health, household composition, and job access; this is not a standardized or causal contrast.
observations.subgroup: Persons not reporting a work-limiting condition in the first month
observations.counterinterpretation: A higher job-count-change share among lower-resource persons without a reported limitation does not establish greater opportunity or voluntary mobility.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month t job-count category to month t+1 resource-band change; work-limiting status = yes

denominator.unit: valid adjacent person-month pairs with positive person weight and a documented work-limiting condition

zero_jobs_resource_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.128 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 2.125–2.625

one_job_resource_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.351 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 4.583–5.959

two_jobs_resource_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.167 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 3.449–8.023

three_or_more_jobs_resource_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 4.049 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 1.990–17.863

observations.method: Reverse same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag from RMNUMJOBS to THINCPOV, conditioned on EDISABL=yes; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Census Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: The three-or-more-job condition cell is sparse and imprecise. Job count is not hours, pay, schedule control, job quality, or voluntary choice.
observations.counterinterpretation: More resource movement after multiple jobs may reflect earnings, hours, transfers, household changes, or costs rather than job-count effects.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month t job-count category to month t+1 resource-band change; work-limiting status = no

denominator.unit: valid adjacent person-month pairs with positive person weight and no reported work-limiting condition

zero_jobs_resource_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.125 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 2.996–3.487

one_job_resource_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.124 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 3.382–3.868

two_jobs_resource_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.341 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 4.275–5.612

three_or_more_jobs_resource_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.219 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 2.537–7.316

observations.method: Reverse same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag from RMNUMJOBS to THINCPOV, conditioned on EDISABL=no; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Census Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: This is a descriptive contrast with composition and measurement differences; the person-level replicate weights do not create a household estimate.
observations.subgroup: Persons not reporting a work-limiting condition
observations.counterinterpretation: Resource-band movement among people with multiple jobs may reflect earnings and household conditions rather than greater security or control.

related_sources.claim: The SIPP work-limiting status and resource layer defines EDISABL and its cross-sectional boundary.

boundary: Same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag conditioned on the reported work-limiting status field. It does not establish causality, household prevalence, disability diagnosis, accommodation, job quality, pay, care, trust, political action, or recovery.
